steps.body: When two numbers have the same tens, compare the ones. 63 vs 67: both have 6 tens, so look at the ones — 3 is less than 7, so 63 < 67.
Use the line to break a tens tie.

widget.prompt: The marker starts at 63. Drag it to 67.

commonPlacements.feedback: 66 is one spot before 67. The tens still tie, so keep counting the ones.
68 is one spot after 67. Move one spot left.

widget.successFeedback: 67 sits to the right of 63. With the same 6 tens, 7 ones is more than 3 ones.
widget.lowFeedback: The marker is below 67. Move right.
widget.highFeedback: The marker is above 67. Move left.

predict.prompt: 63 and 67 have the same tens. Where will 67 sit compared with 63?
predict.reveal: The marker moves right from 63 to 67. The tens tie, so the larger ones digit makes 67 greater.

widget.gtFeedback: Tens are equal (6 each). Compare ones: 3 < 7, so 63 < 67.
widget.eqFeedback: Same tens, but the ones differ (3 vs 7), so 63 < 67, not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — tens tie at 6, and 3 ones is less than 7 ones, so 63 < 67.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — tens tie at 5, and 8 ones is more than 4 ones, so 58 > 54.
widget.ltFeedback: Tens are equal (5 each). Compare ones: 8 > 4, so 58 > 54.

steps.body: Always check the tens first; only when they match do the ones decide. 71 and 76 both have 7 tens, so 1 < 6 means 71 < 76.

widget.gtFeedback: Tens are equal (7 each). Compare ones: 1 < 6, so 71 < 76.
widget.eqFeedback: Same tens, but the ones differ (1 vs 6), so 71 < 76, not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — tens tie at 7, and 1 one is less than 6 ones, so 71 < 76.

steps.body: If the tens and the ones are both the same, the numbers are equal. 45 = 45. That's when you use the = sign.

widget.gtFeedback: 45 isn't greater than 45 — the tens match (4 = 4) and the ones match (5 = 5), so they're equal.
widget.ltFeedback: 45 isn't less than 45 — the tens match (4 = 4) and the ones match (5 = 5), so they're equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — same tens and same ones, so 45 = 45.

steps.body: When tens tie, the ones decide — and matching both means equal.
takeaways: Same tens and same ones means the numbers are equal.
Use = only when every digit matches.
